quest.title: Spell of Unity
quest.description: Everyone decided to do something after hearing about how badly the last Bloomflower Trials went, and what happened to the little Qucusaur Antu. However, you'll need help from your other friends...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Mora x40000, Crown of Insight x1

chapter.num: Tournament of Glory in Bloom: Act III
chapter.title: Spell of Unity

talks.objective: Meet in the Speaker's Chamber to discuss the plan

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: *yawn*... So sleepy!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Didn't sleep well?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Yeah... I blame Kachina, being all mysterious about some gathering to discuss "something important." I was so curious, I couldn't stop tossing and turning the whole night!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Also, how come it's so quiet today? You didn't lock Ajaw up, did you?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: When I tried to wake him up this morning, his response was: "Leave me be, minion! Dar'st thou disturb the Almighty Dragonlord in our slumber?" I figured it'd be for the best that he's not here anyway, so I didn't bother calling him again.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Haha, good thing you didn't tell him about our gathering. We could do without his gate-crashing, for sure...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Not late, am I?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Nope, you're right on time. So, Ifa, now that everyone's here, shall we begin?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: *ahem*... Actually, today we have a big favor we'd like to ask of all of you.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: What's up? Why so serious all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: It's... a long story. One that begins with a "mysterious friend" of Milray's...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Ifa relates what happened in the Bloomflower Trials centuries ago, and the tale of the little Qucusaur, Antu.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After hearing such a tragic tale, everyone seems a bit gloomy.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Bloodshed between the tribes... That seems almost unthinkable today, but it was an everyday occurrence in that era.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Even working together on something was impossible... That's just too awful!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: There have always been disputes, but once they escalated into fully-fledged clashes between tribes... Even a peacemaker would have been powerless to mediate.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: And that little Qucusaur, Antu, believed that the Sacred Flame Crystals harbored some kind of evil power that lay at the root of these inter-tribal conflicts.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: And that led to all the later misunderstandings. At this point, it would be nigh impossible to explain the truth to him... Granny's right, it would only make him suffer all over again.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That said, Antu will naturally sense that something's off once we've collected enough Sacred Flame Crystals and cure Milray, won't he?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: He'll see that no one has been "corrupted" and that all is as it should be. At that point, he would realize the truth of what happened in the past, even as young as he is.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Exactly. That's why we came up with a plan.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: When the second half of the tournament wraps up, we'll have enough Sacred Flame Crystals. That's when I want everyone to act like the Crystals have messed with us and start arguing.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Ooh, acting! That sounds fun. Then what?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Then, we'll bring Antu over and cast a "Spell of Unity" to cleanse all the bad vibes within the Sacred Flame Crystals and bring everyone back to their senses.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Of course, neither the evil power or the magic are real, but we've gotta make the lil' dude think he's done "something awesome."

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Aha, yeah. I get where you're going with this.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: The best way to make up for regrets is to do what you failed to do before. We'll recreate that scene from his past, only this time, he'll get the chance to rewrite the future.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: So, how exactly are we going to do this? Is there anything we can look to?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Once, when I was reading a foreign book, I came across something called an "interactive play," designed specifically for kids.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The story usually features a showdown between a hero and a villain, with twists and turns throughout. Just as things reach a climax, the hero will pretend to be losing and ask for the children's help.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Then, the children all raise their hands, lending their power to the hero and helping them defeat the villain.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: For the adults watching, it's just a performance, but the children will walk away feeling happy for days to come.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: At that age, happiness doesn't come from material rewards, but from "a heart that believes."

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: True! I can totally relate.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: When I helped out at my parents' shop as a kid, they would always intentionally leave me some simple tasks, like dusting down the shelves or making sure the merchandise was arranged neatly.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Then they'd shower me with praise when I was finished, saying stuff like, "Good job, Mualani, you're a genius!"... And the funny thing is, it always made me super happy!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Spot on, that's exactly it. We wanna make Antu feel the same way a kid who just helped a hero would, lessen his regret and pain... before he moves on.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Besides, Milray already heard the rumors about the Sacred Flame Crystals from him. If we don't dispel the "curse" right in front of him, he might refuse to take the medicine.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: But we can't pull off a show like that with just us. That's why I'm asking for your help.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: We'll probably need about five more people... *ahem* I mean, there are five more spots up for grabs. First come, first served!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: You have my board! Hehe, I'm probably the best at arguing here, don'cha think?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: We get some pretty rude customers in our shop, and I've had to develop quite a few communication skills to deal with them.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: You have my... cabbages? I can help prepare some props and special effects, like smoke to mimic the "evil power" and bright lights for the "Spell of Unity."

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: And my Flamestrider.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Oh, you're joining too, Archon?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: It really resonated with me when Citlali mentioned a clash between heroes and villains.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: And unlike the heroes in those plays, I've borrowed strength from all of you in the real world — and we've overcome powerful foes together as a result. I think I'll do justice to the role.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: If Mavuika's on board, then you have my hammer. I'm really interested in the part where we "pretend to argue."

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Let's see. We've got our actors, and the stage is set. Now, we need a... director. A dude to run the show.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Why are you all looking at me?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Consider it our vote of confidence, Kinich!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Fine. Then you have my grappling hook. I happen to have some time.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: So that's everyone, then? In that case, Varesa and I will take care of the cleanup.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Sorry, guys. I'd love to sign up, but I already promised to help transport the wounded.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: As for me... Ugh, if I see you all arguing, I wouldn't be able to resist stepping in.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: And I'm just really bad at acting. I'd be so stiff, the game would be up before we even got started.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I'll stay and help the saurians search for Ocean Zephyrs. Once they've brought enough back, I'll join you as soon as I can.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: As our Archon herself often says, "we all have our own part to play"... Right?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That's right. Alright, once the second half of the exhibition match is over, we'll split into two teams and play our respective "parts."

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Great! Let's make the second half an even more exciting fight. That way, we'll be able to collect more Sacred Flame Crystals to help cure Milray.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I've even come up with a "secret strategy" that's sure to catch you all off guard!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: After centuries, we're holding the Bloomflower Trials once more. I hope that this time, we can bring them to a close free from regret.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Are you all confident that we can do this?

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Yeah!!!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Then let's get this show on the road!

talks.objective: Participate in the second half of the exhibition match

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, looks like everyone's here. Time for a strategy meeting!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, why do they keep picking battlefields covered in mountains that need climbing...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...But you can fly, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: If you're worried about getting tired, I can just fly you straight to the top.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Launching a surprise attack on their base would also be a good tactic.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I'll use smoke to sow confusion amongst their ranks, then you guys can just charge in and beat the living daylights out of them.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It'll be over as soon as it began.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *ahem* These two are in even more of a rush than Paimon is...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Let's all just calm down for a moment. We don't even know what their formation will be like. Besides, if we don't deal with nearby opponents first, our main base could be at risk.

choices.text: Slow and steady wins the race.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But the area nearby is full of rocks... Looks like they're trying to block our path.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Pff, that's nothing. Let's just charge straight through.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: C'mon, time for a warm-up!

choices.text: Let's start with the base at the foot of the mountain.

talks.objective: Attack the Children of Echoes' base

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I—I'll stop you in your tracks!

talks.objective: Defeat the base guards and switch the flag

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Excellent, we've secured the Children of Echoes' base. Time to head up the mountain.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: All tuckered out? Let me give you a hand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Granny to the rescue! Now that's what Paimon calls some serious backup!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Granny's... not here to check if I've been slacking, is she...?

talks.objective: Attack the People of the Springs' base
Defeat the base guards and switch the flag

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Nice, another one in the bag.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Something's wrong... There are far fewer people in their base than expected.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: And Mualani hasn't put in an appearance yet either...

dialogues.speaker: Sanora
dialogues.text: Uh oh, not good! The People of the Springs took back the base we just captured.

dialogues.speaker: Sanora
dialogues.text: And even worse, they're sending troops to attack our main base...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hah. That girl has some moves, I'll give her that...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Looks like we'll have to split our forces to hold off their counterattack.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'll handle Mualani. She still owes me for wrecking my front door. You just focus on moving forward.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: You're a lifesaver, Granny Citlali. We can rest easy knowing you're here covering the rear.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Thanks, Granny. We've got this.

talks.objective: Attack the Scions of the Canopy's base

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I knew that wouldn't stop you. Let's have our weapons do the talking.

talks.objective: Defeat the base guards and switch the flag

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: The fruits of victory taste almost as sweet as ones I've grown myself... At least I won't be in for one of Granny's scoldings.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well that explains why you were so fired up today...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ororon... Since when has your Granny ever gone around scolding people like some sort of scary monster, huh? Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Ahem, anyway... Good workout, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: You can say that again. It's not every day you get to enjoy the thrill of battle.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You youngsters sure love a good brawl, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Once this is all over, I think I'll need a few days at home to lie down and recover...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Thanks, Granny. Without your support, who knows what might have happened.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hmph, I'll have you know that Mualani didn't pull any punches during our little skirmish just now.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Next time she shows up at my place asking for a favor, I'm giving her a proper talking-to...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, shows that everyone really was giving it their all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, after all that, surely we've collected enough Sacred Flame Crystals now?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: We have indeed. Let's gather them up and head back.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Next up, time for our little "play."

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ifa, this should be enough, right?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Yeah, plenty, maybe more than we can even use.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That's great news. Just goes to show how fired up everyone was. Let's set the remainder aside in case of emergency.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Next up, the main event. When do we start?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Just a sec. Before we roll the kameras, let's break it all down one more time.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Shortly, you'll all take the Sacred Flame Crystals and place them in front of Milray and Naiyan. Then, once Kinich gives the signal, Ororon will do his thing, and the Crystals will start giving off a black mist.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: That'll be the cue to start fighting. Once things get real heated, we'll bring Antu in and have him cast the "Spell of Unity."

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Afterwards, Ororon will clear his black mist, and then we all go back to chillin' with each other. Any questions?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Relax, I've played it all through in my head many times now.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Great. Then let's do this.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Phew. Finally, we've got all the Sacred Flame Crystals we need. Don't worry, little guy, you'll be better in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: Wroooh...

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: Rawrrrrrr!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's just like Ifa said — he looks very reluctant to go through with this...

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: Wrrawr...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: As long as he sees us "dispel the curse" with his own eyes, we'll be alright... Let's proceed.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Hey, Mualani! Ugh, that's weird, I feel a bit... dizzy...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: (Special Effects team, get in position.)

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (On the case.)

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Now, time to get squabbling. As agreed, we'll start with Mualani.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: You've got this, Mualani...!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Leave it to me!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: *ahem* Now listen up, Kachina—

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I, uhh... I—I'm gonna give you a piece of my mind, ya hear me? I'd never have thought you'd do something so terrible, Kachina! Why, I'm positively furious!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Eh? Wh—What did I do again?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That... is a good question! Let me... think about that...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: ...I thought you said you were a natural at this?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I—I am! But... I'm struggling to come up with a reason to argue! How am I supposed to tap into old talents when I'm drawing blanks here...

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: Rrrarawwr?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: If this goes on much longer, even the little saurians will realize something's off.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Don't get caught up on the reasons for an argument! Just start by setting the atmosphere for one!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Don't panic, I'm thinking, I'm thinking... I know! How about this...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Kachina! You stand accused of the heinous crime of eating my very last Saurus Cracker!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Ehhh?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: When we went out for a picnic last night, you ate the last Saurus Cracker! How could you have done such an abominable thing? I was saving that for the end!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: O—Oh! I'm sorr— Uh, I mean, so? You ate way more than I did...!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: No, no, no! You just don't get it! The ones we ate in the middle don't matter — the last one's always the tastiest!

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: Wrraawr...?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Good, he's starting to buy it. Time to turn up the heat.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Mualani, isn't it about time you paid up for wrecking my door?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Seriously, you're bringing this up now!? You promised to let it go the last time we had dinner together!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: And when might that have been?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: The last time we had dinner, like I said! We were over at the People of the Springs, and you'd had just a teensy bit too much to drink... You took my hand and said it was "all water under the bridge"!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hold on, have you genuinely forgotten? This isn't part of your act, is it? And to think, I tried so hard...

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: Roarrr!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Is this... what Sacred Flame Crystals can do? It's like you've all become completely different people.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Surely, our only hope now is for me to—

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Can it, Mavuika! Do you even have any idea how long I've had to put up with your nonsense?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Without so much as a heads up, you just dump some pile of design schematics in my workshop that you'd gotten from who knows where, then tell me to build you that... Flamerider, or whatever you call it!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Then you drive it into the wilderness every single day, then whenever it breaks down, you send it straight back to me for repair — even when I'm on vacation!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Oh, and not to mention your special sunglasses and that precious sword of yours that's impervious to even the hottest of flames... Do you need me to make a list?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Is it just me, or is Xilonen's acting pretty convincing?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: She might be the only one who's not actually acting, Kachina.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: *yawn*... So sleepy. Why didn't you wake me up this morning, Kinich?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: From now on, I'm not taking any more work during holidays, and you're banned from showing up at my vacation spots.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Wait a minute, I remember now! You were the one who kept encouraging me to drink more that evening!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Trying to get me drunk so you could write off some old debts, huh? Smooth moves, Mualani! Figured out some tricks to use on old Granny, have you?

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Well, well, would you look at that! All these little pipsqueaks suddenly at each other's throats? What a golden opportunity this could be—

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Listen up, everyone! Arguing won't solve any problems, so let's settle this with a good old-fashioned fight to the death! I, the Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw, hereby appoint myself your referee!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Kinich, let's start with Kinich! Who's got it in for Kinich?

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Wh—What's wrong? Why are you all looking at me?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Perfect timing.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: You! Well, you're the worst! You wasted an entire bucket of ice by taking a BATH in it!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: And you ate all those crackers I baked! I spent the whole night preparing them...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Always yelling at the top of your lungs — you're a permanent earache in a pint-sized package!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: No list would suffice to record the horrible things you've done.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa, time out, time out! Why's this all suddenly aimed at me?

dialogues.speaker: Milray & Naiyan
dialogues.text: Raaaawr...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: H—How could this be? The argument's spiraling out of control! I can no longer cleanse the evil power within the Sacred Flame Crystals myself!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: If this goes on much longer... Continues for much longer... Uhh, how does it go again... Let me see...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Oh yeah. "If this goes on much longer, Natlan will be in grave danger."

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: "We're so close. If only a brave hero would step forward..."

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: (Good thing I wrote that all down in advance. Hopefully I sold it...)

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: That's us! You ready, Antu?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: ...Antu?

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: There's no need to save him. Think of what we could accomplish with all those Sacred Flame Crystals.

dialogues.speaker: Shanga
dialogues.text: Fine by me! Let's settle our old scores today, once and for all!

dialogues.speaker: Shanga
dialogues.text: What right do you Children of Echoes think you have to point fingers at us? How many times have you wronged us over the years?

dialogues.speaker: Monetech
dialogues.text: Bunch of liars and cowards, banding together like the vermin you are. It's sickening.

dialogues.speaker: Tepanahui
dialogues.text: Never have the heavens smiled down upon those who live by the rules. If something's worth having, you've got to take it by force.

dialogues.speaker: Paio
dialogues.text: I should never have believed you!

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: (It's all my fault... If only I'd never fallen ill in the first place...)

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: (I don't want to be cured, and I don't want the Sacred Flame Crystals. Please stop fighting, please!)

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Guguu... Crrawr...

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Antu!

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: You're up, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: ...Crraaaaa!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This ends now! We're here to save the day!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Evil power that corrupts the human heart, there's no place for you in Natlan anymore!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: We will stand united and face the years ahead together.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Fly, my dude, fly! Cast the "Spell of Unity," just like I taught you!

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Gruuuu!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: (Now, Ororon.)

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (Got it.)

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: "The path of fate lies bleak. Walls rise in human hearts."

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: "Yet those walls we shall break, and we will march on."

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: "From this day forth, may worldly strife be no more—"

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Gugugu—!!!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: What in the... Look, the evil power is fading.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The magic's working.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Grainfruit Chips taste so much better with sweet cheese — that's not even up for debate!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hmph, I think you'll find that salted cheese is the classic — the first and best choice in Natlan for centuries.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Pfff, cheese? That stuff's for kids, I'd never go near it!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Well, I guess you're not completely wrong! They have a unique flavor with salted cheese too — the perfect storytime snack.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Also great with a glass of wine. Though sweet cheese with a splash of liqueur works well too...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Let's have another get-together sometime. Don't worry, I won't bring up the door incident again.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: You're amazing, Granny! Next time, I'll come with Kachina, and we'll bring some home-baked Saurus Crackers and Grainfruit Chips along...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: And some Blazed Meat Stew and Volcano Cake, too!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Sure! In that case, I'll go find Varesa and we'll make you some nice... juice, or something. *sigh* When will you all grow up? Why does it feel like I'm always the only one drinking...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: You should stay off the bottle, too, Granny! Isn't there some kind of sweet and sour soup that's all the rage with the Masters of the Night-Wind right now? What's it called again... Mystique Soup? Much better than alcohol, if you ask me!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Wait a minute, what exactly is going on here? Your attitudes towards each other are changing way too fast!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: That's weird... What was I just saying?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I can't remember for the life of me... Can you, Mavuika?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hmm, something about wishing I dropped by your workshop more often, and how grateful you are that I keep pushing you to achieve the impossible...?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: "Life is like climbing a mountain — all the best views are at the top." You just give people that kind of... vibe.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: ...Wait, are you serious?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Just kidding! I'll... try my best not to dump any more strange commissions on you.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: How in Teyvat have you two...

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Snap out of it, people! It's like you're all under some kind of spell! Quick, Kinich, think of something—

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Ajaw... I owe you an apology, too. I've been too harsh on you.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: It seems the evil power is completely gone. Were you the one who helped us?

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Cuuu!

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Awesome job, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Great job, Antu. Now that the Sacred Flame Crystals have been cleansed, we can use them to cure your friend.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Don't leave him hanging, go tell him the good news!

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: Rawr?

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Cucuuu!

dialogues.speaker: Milray & Naiyan
dialogues.text: Raaawr...

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Thank you so much, all of you. This turned out even better than I imagined.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: See, told you it would all work out! Didn't I mention I'm an old hand at this whole argument game?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: You were this close to spilling the beans.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hear, hear! Even the kids of our tribe would have done a better job. Tell you what, we're lucky they don't speak our language...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I couldn't help it! Besides, how was I supposed to, you know, criticize Kachina to her face like that?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Mualani...! Actually, it was the same for me... Even though I knew it was all just an act, I didn't want to argue with you.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Huh? So you were all just playing pretend? Ugh, boooring. I'm going back to bed.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Don't let the door hit you on the way out.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Now all that's left are the Ocean Zephyrs, right? I heard on the way over that we'd already found some, so it shouldn't take long...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Everyone, over here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Iansan! And... Whoa, that's a lot of saurians!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: We've gathered enough Ocean Zephyrs! I asked them to give them to me, but they wanted to bring them over themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: So we came together. Here, I think this should be enough.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Just hang on a moment, everyone. I'll go mix the ingredients.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Hey, Cacucu, dude! Less chat, more help.

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Sure thing, bro. I've got you, bro.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Ifa quickly prepares the medicine and feeds it to Milray.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Now comes the most important step of all...

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Phew... This is it. The moment we've all been waiting for.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: O' Sacred Flame Crystal, forged by the will of many... Please, work your wonders and drive this sickness away.

talks.objective: Talk to Ifa and the others

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: Rawrrr...

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Cheer up, bro. It's always tough to lose a friend, but in this case, our parting is their reunion.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Antu's already wandered the world for way too long, but now that you're all fixed up, he can be at peace.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: His final wish was to be reunited with his bro, and he's done that. We should be happy for him, just like he celebrated your recovery.

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: Wrrooah!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Thanks a ton, everyone. With your help, I've been able to do what my ancestor could not.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Not only did we save this little saurian from his torment, we also made a historic contribution to the study of phlogiston-related diseases.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: ...As a physician, I'm honestly feeling touched and overwhelmed.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Well said. Then without further ado, I hereby announce that the Bloomflower Trials have come to a successful close!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: From my perspective, though, this competition had another meaning. Throughout the event, I didn't witness any arguments, scheming, or plotting for personal gain. All six tribes united to accomplish something truly remarkable.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Even without the threat of the Abyss, we're still as close as family. We've surpassed those who came before us, and in the future, our people will surely grow more united still.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: So, in keeping with our traditions... It's time for a celebration. Let's make this a lively one, people!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani & Paimon
dialogues.text: Woohoo!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: As it happens, I picked a whole batch of fresh vegetables just yesterday. I'll go get them now.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Leave the meat to me.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: And don't you dare skimp on it, Kinich.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I'll go gather the others. Many hands make light work, and besides, the best meals are always ones prepared together.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: See you tonight, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: See you tonight! Hehe, Paimon's ready for a feast and a half...

talks.objective: Take part in the celebration banquet

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kachina!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Hehe, fancy a slice of Volcano Cake? I baked it myself!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oooh, in that case, Paimon'd be glad to oblige!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... good... Hehe, Paimon's tempted to eat the whole cake!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Go ahead! I made this specially for you guys!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Sweet cakes help people forget their worries, and I hope everyone can be happy every day!

choices.text: You seem to have bounced back, Kachina.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Yep, I'm feeling much better! I definitely was unsure about where my future lay for a while there.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: But reading through those old scrolls, I realized that the six tribes haven't always been so united. They used to argue a lot, and even got into big fights...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I've never experienced anything like that. I can barely imagine such a harsh way of life.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I love Natlan the way it is today, and I love spending time with my friends! As Uncle Pacal once told me, the harder something is to come by, the more we should treasure it.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: So I've decided to always do my best to help and make sure my friends are happy. Most importantly, I want us all to stay united, forever and ever!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I haven't figured out exactly how I'm gonna do that... But I can start with what I'm good at, like baking delicious crackers and cakes to share with everyone!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y'know what, Paimon just had an idea. You could open a cake shop!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That way, Paimon would be able to enjoy your cakes even more often than she already does...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: You really think so? I'll have to get Mualani to teach me how to run a shop then...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Baking delicious desserts every day and making everyone smile... That does sound like a wonderful life!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Thanks guys! I think I might've found a new goal to work towards.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By the way, Paimon hasn't seen Ifa or that Qucu-Thesaurus yet. Any idea where they went?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Before the party, I heard he was planning on heading up that hill to pay respects to his ancestor. They're not back yet?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If he doesn't get back soon, all the best food's gonna be gone!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess we've got no choice but to take the cake with us and go check on them...

choices.text: I'll be rooting for you all the way!
I see the cloud hanging over your head during the competition has disappeared.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Yo, ancestor man. Guess you're reunited with Antu already?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: I have a Qucusaur companion too, so I totally get how you must've felt.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: First time I saw this dude, he was out in the wild, being bullied by other saurians because of his unusual appearance. He'd been pecked all over the place, bleeding from head to toe...

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: He barely made it. I gave him some meds, and from then on, he just stuck to me like glue. Even wound up becoming my assistant.

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Thanks, bro.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Hey, don't mention it, dude.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Being on the road with me as a vet was never gonna be an easy gig. One time, when we were treating a sick saurian, Cacucu got infected too.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: He ran a high fever, and I searched everywhere for ingredients and did everything I could for him. But despite giving it my all, he was right on the edge, man... and all I could do was keep praying.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: If he hadn't recovered, I know I'd have felt the same guilt you did.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Luckily, he managed to pull through, and he even stayed by my side helping me ever since. He's a solid assistant, no question.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: So yeah, Cacucu, I'm the one who should be thanking you.

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Hey, don't mention it, dude.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Your "medicine born of guilt"... Don't sweat it. We'll keep improving it as we go. You have my word.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: That way, no one else will ever have to feel the same guilt that you did, ever again.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Huh? Yo, bros, what brings you guys here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Bringing our bros some cake, of course! Kachina made these herself, ya know — they're incredible!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: For real? In that case, I gotta—

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Oh wow, that's awesome, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Hey, save some for me!

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: The more meat you eat, the faster you'll recover!

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: Roarrr!

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: Rooooarrr!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: A toast — to the successful conclusion of the Bloomflower Trials! Cheers!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Cheers! Finally, a few days off.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Planning a vacation, are we?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Judging from my experience with the Pilgrimage, things are pretty quiet for a few days after competitions. There usually isn't much trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Yeah, competitions do take a lot out of everyone. We all need a good rest.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Cheers to that, and a long-overdue break.

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: Try some, try some! How do they taste?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Delicious, as always. It's your signature dish, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Yum!

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: This wine's amazing.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Of course! Wouldn't have made it into my collection otherwise.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Drink as much as you like today, people. I mean, I owe you all one, don't I?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: We might just have to take you up on that.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: As much as we like? Haha, you might regret saying that!

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Ahem... Uhh... Alright, bring it on!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I've kept the extra Sacred Flame Crystals for future use. Next time you need some, just come to me.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Also... This was my first time "acting" in a play like this. I find I really enjoyed it. What did you think of my acting skills?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Mmm, I'd have to agree with that. Seems like I still have a lot to learn.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Is it something you're good at? Some tips would be nice if we find a suitable time for it.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Oh really? Well then, next time something like this comes up, don't forget to keep me in the loop.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I'm curious — how did you create that black mist?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: It was just an illusion. If Granny had been the one doing it, she could've come up with something much more impressive.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, you can stop with the flattery. "Just an illusion?" Hmph, you're already good enough to fool me.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Oh... Err, is that incident still on your mind? I didn't exactly have a choice back then...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Relax, I'm not here to dig up the past. I'm just saying you've got a real knack for illusions — and that's something to be proud of!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Thanks, Granny.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: "I owe you an apology, too. I've been too harsh on you."

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: *sigh* Wish I could've frozen that moment in time, so you could just listen to yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: A few more drinks, and who knows — you might hear it again, in your dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Want some more cake? I made plenty!
